summary: Apply rock-strength and wellbore-stability methods to drilling decisions. Review mud-weight and ECD cases in this five-day course. Explore the outline.
lede: Geomechanics and rock mechanics connect rock strength, stress and pore pressure to wellbore stability and drilling decisions. For drilling engineers, wellsite supervisors and geomechanics analysts, the course develops practical skills to assess instability, estimate rock strength and interpret stress and pore-pressure evidence. You will apply Mohr-Coulomb and Hoek-Brown criteria, assess mud-weight limits and ECD against stability risks, and document drilling recommendations with stated assumptions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use rock and well data to plan, monitor, or troubleshoot drilling operations. It suits those who need to connect geomechanical evidence with practical wellbore-stability and drilling decisions.
prerequisites: Intermediate level. Prior experience in drilling, well planning, wellsite operations, or geoscience is expected, along with familiarity with basic drilling terminology and well logs. No coding or programming is required.
